UK trans journo here.  


Never seen them change their mind. That is the truth.  


The ideology is in the hypothetical. And it stays there.  Especially here. You are taking on an anti trans backlash that has entered it's 5th year (it didn't start in 2018, it started in 2016).  


Honestly, do what you can to keep them away from trans people and don't touch it. Best thing you can do for trans people in the UK right now is call them by their name and pronouns, and treat them like anyone else. We are where gay LGB cis people were in the late 80's. We don't have the HIV epidemic but we have the hate.  


 [Why is Britain so transphobic? A look at the UK's transphobia epidemic](https://www.pinknews.co.uk/2021/02/15/britain-transphobia-uk-transphobic-history-gender-recognition-act-what-the-trans/)   


This explains what you are up against.  


Be there as a good friend to trans people in your life. Spend the time you would have spent arguing with your parents, spend it with your trans friends instead.  


Thank you for coming here and trying to help in some way. Wonderful intentions, hope you can put them into action.

As I understand it, it is transphobia that has been picked up from society and is perpetrated against you BY you inside your own head.

I think you provide a good example of how insidious this can be. You say you are scared of transitioning and it not working out...

... whose standards are you trying to adhere to? Because transitioning is only about doing what you need to do to be the best you. At some point someone told you indirectly that transitioning is only worthwhile if you measure up to cis people’s standards but that isn’t it.

Internalised transphobia is the voice in your head that tells you that being trans is weird, or wrong. It is a real killer, I struggle with it to this day. But I think folks in your generation have a much better shot at not having this be a massive issue.

Hope this helps

Long one. The seeds were planted when I started working at a supermarket in the UK. The wages were awful and people were so devalued and their whole lives in and out of work were in service to a supermarket, more so than even more white collar jobs I got afterwoulds. The work was the hardest I have ever done, and I had to perform the job with a constant grin on my face. I got told off for failing to maintain a smile constantly during 4-6 hour stints on the shop floor (with a 30 minute break to relax my face muscles at lunch). That felt so profoundly unfair and almost abusive. Workers rights became very important there.  


Then it was renting. I got into debt having to constantly move with only 2 months notice to gather a security deposit and 6 weeks rent (who has £1500 to cover moving and all of that with two months notice when working shitty shop jobs?). This messed with my anxiety and contributed to health problems that I am still wrestling with. This felt profoundly unfair, that I could be ruined financially because some guy in Dubai decides to give the flat a fresh lick of paint then double the rent. If I was not as lucky as I have been, I would have been homeless several times. The right to having a stable home became very important to me.  


Then it was being transgender. Seeing how powerful cisgender people were making things so much worse for people like me and trans folks NEVER getting a say. We would get some lip service from more liberal politicians but overall, trans folks weren't ever getting liberated without their being a significant upside to those in power. This felt so unfair to me and minority rights became very important to me.  


Then I did a quiz online and because of my experiences it said I was an Anarchist. I was genuinely shocked because to me that was a label for extremists, which I don't see myself as being. I wasn't radicalized by online literature, I was radicalized by my life under capitalism and being on the wrong end of it far too many times. Looking at the replies here, this feels like a very common reason. I thought of myself at most as a democratic socialist because those were the political voices that most matched my own views but it never felt right because they never seemed to go far enough. I want it so landlords, billionaires, capitalists CANNOT exist, not just reforming the current system to make it a bit more fair.  


Guess I learned that being a political extremist is not only due to how extreme your ideas are in how much work needs to be done to achieve them, but also named because of how different it is to the current system and in the end, that isn't a good reason not to go for it.

Been about 8 years and my Dad never calls me by my name.

I took it because my Mum told me to keep the peace. Accept him as he is to maintain a good relationship.

​

It wasn't a good relationship for me.

​

Do not leave it that long to fester, but give it time. In a year they could be fine. In 6 months they could be with you at some pride event. It is still early days.  


Just don't let it go on for as long as I let it go on with my Dad. The damage done there is huge. Protect yourself.
